correctness.rationale: Differentiation gives g_i=e3(hat i)= -H(x_i), where H(T)=T^3-e1T^2+e2T-e3. If all derivatives vanish, every coordinate is among <=3 roots of H. Newton sums 1,2,3 for the coordinate multiset and roots of H agree. Vandermonde in the distinct nonzero roots forces their coordinate multiplicities to equal root multiplicities, so at most three coordinates are nonzero; for n>=6 a coordinate zero implies H(0)=0, reducing bound to two. Conversely two-support points are singular. As the singular locus consists of lines, projective hypersurface cannot be reducible or nonreduced; by R1/S2 it is integral normal. Near a general coordinate line [a:b:0:...], quadratic e4=ab e2(z)+higher and Hessian determinant (-1)^(n-3)(n-3)(ab)^(n-2) nonzero. The n=6 split 4-variable completed quadric has class group Z, while for n>=7 local CI rings are regular through height 3 and Samuel–Grothendieck parafactorial/factoriality applies to all localizations; no claim that n=6 algebraic local rings are nonfactorial. Independent exact SymPy Hessian at a=2,b=3 produced -3888 for n6 and 31104 for n7 and checked noncritical points on all 3/4-support signed bounded integer vectors (5120 and 11200). These finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: A natural fundamental symmetric quartic exhibits an exact all-n singular-support classification and sharp formal class-group/local factoriality transition between n=6 and n>=7; its exact codimension computation is essential to apply the classical factoriality theorem, beyond a trivial restatement of it.

final_claim: For characteristic-zero algebraically closed k and every n>=6, the projective e4(x1,...,xn)=0 hypersurface is integral normal with reduced singular locus precisely the binomial(n,2) coordinate lines. Along each line the generic transverse quadratic form e2 on n-2 variables is nondegenerate; for n=6 its completed generic transverse ring is a four-variable ordinary quadric cone with class group Z, while for n>=7 every algebraic local ring is factorial and the higher-dimensional generic quadratic completions are factorial.
limitations: Reduced set support and generic germs; full Jacobian scheme not analyzed.
